blocks.text: Built a RAG-powered dental billing audit system that extracts structured data from Explanation of Benefits documents, retrieves relevant insurance policy and reimbursement rules, and produces evidence-backed discrepancy flags for human review. Reduced per-claim review time from 15 minutes to under 1 minute while improving consistency and explainability.
Problem

Dental EOBs are difficult to interpret because payment logic depends on plan-specific policies, fee schedules, coverage limits, exclusions, deductibles, annual maximums, and procedure-level reimbursement rules. Manual review is slow, inconsistent, and hard to scale.
Patients often cannot tell whether a claim was paid correctly without understanding plan-specific rules.
Billing teams reviewing high volumes frequently miss discrepancies under time pressure.
Relevant policy language is buried in lengthy plan documents — not surfaced at the point of review.
No scalable system existed to compare claim outcomes against authoritative reimbursement rules.
Users & Stakeholders

items.title: Patients
items.description: Trying to understand whether they were billed or reimbursed correctly by their dental plan.

items.title: Dental Billing Teams
items.description: Reviewing reimbursement accuracy at high volume with limited time per claim.

items.title: Support Staff
items.description: Explaining claim outcomes and resolving disputes with payers.

items.title: Operators
items.description: Triaging ambiguous flags and managing escalation workflows for complex cases.

blocks.text: Product Goal
Reduce the time required to review an EOB while improving consistency and explainability — without pretending every claim can be fully automated.
Solution

A hybrid AI audit workflow combining document parsing, structured rule checks, RAG over imported policy documents, and LLM reasoning for ambiguous cases. Each finding is grounded in retrievable policy evidence and routed to human review when confidence is low.

items.title: EOB Parsing
items.description: Extracts structured claim fields: procedure codes, billed amounts, allowed amounts, paid amounts, patient responsibility, and deductible applied.

items.title: Policy Knowledge Base
items.description: Imported dental insurance policies, CDT code documentation, fee schedules, coverage rules, exclusions, and reimbursement guidelines into a searchable vector store.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
items.description: Retrieves the most relevant policy sections and fee schedule entries to ground LLM reasoning in authoritative source language.

items.title: Rules Engine
items.description: Deterministic checks for known billing patterns: duplicate codes, unbundling, frequency limit violations, and missing prior authorizations.

items.title: Discrepancy Flags
items.description: Produces 1–3 prioritized, evidence-backed findings per EOB with supporting policy citations and confidence scores.

items.title: Human Review Routing
items.description: Low-confidence or high-risk findings are routed to human reviewers rather than surfaced as definitive conclusions.

blocks.text: Audit Workflow
RAG Knowledge Base

Policy documents were chunked by benefit category, procedure code range, limitation type, exclusion, and reimbursement rule — making retrieval precise enough to support claim-level reasoning rather than returning irrelevant plan boilerplate.

blocks.title: Policy Knowledge Base — Document Types Indexed

blocks.text: Evaluation & Quality Controls
Built a labeled evaluation set of EOBs with expected discrepancy findings to measure system output against ground truth.
Measured extraction accuracy for structured claim fields (procedure codes, amounts, patient responsibility).
Evaluated retrieval relevance: whether retrieved policy chunks matched the claim's actual benefit category and procedure type.
Checked explanation faithfulness: whether stated reasons cited real, retrievable policy language.
Added confidence thresholds so low-confidence outputs were not surfaced as definitive findings.
Designed human review routing for ambiguous and high-risk cases rather than suppressing them.
Key Product Decisions

blocks.decision: Hybrid rules + LLM vs. pure LLM
blocks.tradeoff: Reimbursement logic requires deterministic checks for known billing violations — LLM alone would miss structured rule failures.
blocks.outcome: Rules engine handles unambiguous violations; LLM handles interpretation of complex and ambiguous policy language.

blocks.tradeoff: Claim decisions depend on plan-specific policy language that changes frequently and varies by payer.
blocks.outcome: RAG over imported policy documents grounds reasoning in source material without requiring retraining as policies change.

blocks.tradeoff: Fully automated adjudication would be faster but harder to verify and difficult to trust in a billing context.
blocks.outcome: Every finding includes supporting policy evidence and a confidence score — outputs are designed for review, not replacement of human judgment.

blocks.decision: Route ambiguous cases vs. hide them
blocks.tradeoff: Surfacing all findings regardless of confidence increases noise and erodes reviewer trust over time.
blocks.outcome: Low-confidence and high-risk findings route to human review rather than appearing as conclusions — keeps precision high.

blocks.text: Before vs. After

blocks.title: Manual Review vs. AI-Assisted Audit
before: Discrepancies easy to miss under time pressure
No policy evidence surfaced at review
after: Policy context retrieved and cited automatically
Consistent structured findings across all claims
Human review focused on ambiguous cases only

blocks.text: Results & Impact
Reduced per-claim review time from 15 minutes to under 1 minute.
Surfaced 1–3 likely discrepancies per reviewed EOB on average.
Created an evidence-backed audit flow with policy citations and confidence scoring on every finding.
Built a simulated evaluation set to validate extraction accuracy, retrieval relevance, and explanation faithfulness.
Demonstrated how RAG-grounded AI can reduce manual review burden while keeping humans in the loop for complex and ambiguous cases.
What I Would Do Next
Build payer-specific policy libraries covering major dental insurance carriers.
Expand CDT procedure code coverage and reimbursement rule depth.
Add batch review mode for billing teams processing high claim volumes.
Track precision and recall across larger labeled evaluation datasets.
Add user feedback loops to improve retrieval quality and discrepancy classification over time.
